records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource key to run bleve.New on the same on-disk directory simultaneously, and the final cache write is last-write-wins. Concurrent initial searches for the same resource (previously serialized by the mutex held across the whole build) race on the same file-backed bleve directory, corrupting the on-disk index or leaking one index handle whose searchers read from a directory the winner later reopens; users get corrupt/empty search results until restart.
records.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` the function `BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the entire build (`b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()`), but the diff removes that and now only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. The code still creates a file-backed index at a deterministic directory path (`dir := filepath.Join(...); index, err = bleve.New(dir, mapper)`), so two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `key` can both run `bleve.New(dir, ...)` and then both build/write documents, with the cache ending up last-write-wins. The diff shows no other synchro

records.issue_text: [BUG] Narrowing the cacheMu critical section in BuildIndex removes the mutual exclusion that serialized concurrent index builds for the same key, so two concurrent calls now both run bleve.New on the same directory and race on the final b.cache[key] write. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource both execute; the loser's index object is silently discarded while its bleve file-backed directory may hold an open writer, and callers that received the discarded index via another path keep querying an index that will never receive updates — under-scoped for a 'performance' change whose new concurrency is neither required by the PR intent nor covered by any test in the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the build-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory (when size > FileThreshold), and the second one fails because the Bleve index path already exists. During server startup with parallel index builds (init previously held this lock across the whole build), a duplicate concurrent BuildIndex for a large namespace returns an error instead of an index, causing Init to fail and — combined with Init now being called from NewResourceServer — the whole ResourceServer constructor to fail; the previous code serialized this correctly.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource key, so two callers race to write b.cache[key] and the loser's index is silently discarded while remaining open. getOrCreateIndex callers that miss the cache concurrently (e.g. an event handler and a background build during search.init) both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory for file-based indexes; the second bleve.New on a directory already open by another index instance fails or corrupts state, and the loser's built index (and its open file handle / mmap) is never closed — leaked file handles plus duplicate full-index builds per race, and the last writer wins so a build with a stale RV can overwrite a newer one in the cache.
